extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of media studies/critical linguistics (A-level to university), journalists and anyone learning to analyse newspaper discourse
extracted.subtask_description: Analysing newspaper discourse and ideology using critical linguistics: identifying news values, selection processes, language choices (syntax, lexis, modality), representation of gender/power, and editorial practices that construct consensus and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values
rubrics_metrics.description: General account of news values that shape what becomes news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how criteria called 'news values' influence selection and prioritisation of events; forms part of the processes of selection and transformation which make up the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias or representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether coverage is bias or representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether reporting presents an unbiased recording of 'hard facts' or constructs a particular representation; encourages scrutiny of implied standpoint and selection effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and analysis of stereotypical representations in news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks at how stereotypes are used in coverage (e.g., of social groups) and how they shape reader understanding and social attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and economic factors in news selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of social and economic actors and forces that influence which stories are selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses the role of institutions, ownership, advertising, and market pressures in shaping news agendas and what is reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship between linguistic choices and how realities are represented in the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws on anthropological linguistics, functional linguistics, variation and social semiotic approaches to show how language mediates reality and constructs representations for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social semiotic in news discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social semiotic tools to analyse news discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies social semiotic analysis to examples of news to reveal meanings produced by linguistic choices and their relation to social context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse and the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: How news discourse addresses and positions the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines reader positioning techniques, implied readership assumptions, and how discourse shapes reader interpretation and consensus formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 'public idiom' and formation of consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: How newspapers establish a public idiom that leads to formation of consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses devices (lexis, narrative framing, recurring metaphors) that help create a shared public language and facilitate consensus or marginalise dissent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus and contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: How news constructs consensus and manages contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigates strategies that resolve, suppress or incorporate contradiction within reporting to maintain coherent narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization and conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of categorization and conversational models in news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies how people/events are categorized (labels, groupings) and how conversational norms/genres are modelled to present stories as commonsense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral models in the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of oral/conversational models as a resource in press writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks at how journalists exploit oral-style features (direct speech, colloquial phrasing) to create authenticity or authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic tools: critical linguistics
rubrics_metrics.description: A suite of linguistic tools for critical analysis of news discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides methodological tools and indicators (see transitivity, syntactic transformations, lexical structure, modality, speech acts) for systematic critique of texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of transitivity choices (process types, participants, agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines how events are represented in clauses (who does what to whom), revealing how agency is assigned or obscured in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntactic transformations of the clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine clause-level transformations and their discursive effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses passivisation, nominalisation and other transformations that can hide actors, reify processes, or shift focus in news narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Study of word choices and lexical patterns shaping meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks at connotations, metaphors, evaluative lexis, naming practices and how lexical selections encode stance and ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal elements: modality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of modality to express certainty, obligation, or attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses modal verbs/adverbs and their deployment to hedge, assert, or attribute responsibility in news statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal elements: speech acts
rubrics_metrics.description: How speech acts (e.g., claims, accusations, promises) operate in news discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies performative utterances and their role in constructing positions, assigning blame, or authorising viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to personalise stories by focusing on individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores how personalisation can individualise systemic issues, privileging human interest angles and obscuring structural causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination and power
rubrics_metrics.description: How discourse encodes discrimination and reflects power relations (gender, class, status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses representations of marginalised groups, the interplay of discrimination and institutional power, and whose interests are foregrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of abuse and of endearment
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of insulting or affectionate terms and their ideological functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines examples (e.g., 'Rambo', 'mad dog') to show how labeling delegitimises or valorises people and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitudes to power / ideological roles of the Press
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how the press positions itself toward power and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether the press reinforces the status quo, challenges authority, or constructs particular ideological roles; includes analysis of 'dominance of the status quo' and portrayals of powerless groups (e.g., hospital patients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Press hysteria / hysterical style
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of sensationalist or hysterical styles in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses rhetorical devices that generate panic or moral panic (case study: the salmonella-in-eggs affair), including chronology, participant construction and hyperbolic framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants and chronology in event coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: How participants and timelines are represented in news events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages mapping of portrayed actors and sequencing to reveal framing choices and causal narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating paradigms / Pandora's box
rubrics_metrics.description: How reporting can introduce, generate and equate new instances and moral panics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses rhetorical moves that create templates (paradigms) for later reporting, e.g., opening 'Pandora's box', assigning blame (e.g., 'Blame the housewife'), and persistence of paradigms over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial voice and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of editorial leadership and the exercise of authority in opinion/leader pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses how editorials 'lead the people' by shaping opinion, deploying authority, and constructing consensus through editorial rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospects for critical news analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflections on methods and future directions for critical analysis of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summative guidance on applying critical linguistic approaches to news and considerations for further work in exposing ideology and practice in the press.
